mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.0% indicates accommodative monetary policy that lowers discount rates and increases equity valuations, producing positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 50% of periods when FEDFUNDS is below 4.0% (measured by 3-year rolling window Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month unemployment rate (UNRATE) increase exceeding 0.3 percentage points signals economic distress that reduces corporate earnings growth, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE rises > 0.3pp in 3 months but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of such instances.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous industrial production decline (INDPRO < 100) and inflation acceleration (CPIAUCSL > 320) signals stagflationary shock that compresses profit margins and increases risk aversion, producing negative S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: INDPRO < 100 and CPIAUCSL > 320 occur but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 55% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In late-cycle expansion regimes, rising CPIAUCSL (inflation) signals central bank rate hikes that reduce equity valuations, causing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days.
failure_condition: CPIAUCSL rises in late-cycle expansion but SPX 20-day returns are positive in more than 60% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: Housing starts (HOUST) above 1500 thousand units signals robust consumer demand for housing, driving positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 days due to sustained economic expansion.
failure_condition: HOUST > 1500 but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of instances.

mechanism_narrative: Low unemployment (UNRATE < 4.0%) combined with strong industrial production (INDPRO > 100) indicates tight labor markets and manufacturing health, boosting corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: UNRATE < 4.0% and INDPRO > 100 hold but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 60% of cases.

mechanism_narrative: In early-cycle recovery regimes, GDP growth (GDPC1) exceeding 1.0% quarterly signals economic expansion, increasing corporate earnings and driving positive S&P 500 returns over 20 days.
failure_condition: GDPC1 growth > 1.0% in early-cycle recovery but SPX 20-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods.

mechanism_narrative: A federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) below 4.0% consistently supports positive short-term equity returns by reducing financing costs and increasing market liquidity over 5 trading days.
failure_condition: FEDFUNDS < 4.0% but SPX 5-day returns are negative in more than 55% of periods (3-year rolling window IC < 0.03).
